topic.DOBRO.ambient 1.x01: Out loud, in front of the panel, and without their parents whispering to them.
topic.DOBRO.ambient 1.x03: Last year a father explained his son’s radio to me better than the son did. The boy just stood there nodding.
topic.DOBRO.ambient 2.label: Why so many forms?
topic.DOBRO.ambient 2.001: A thing can be good and still need three signatures.
topic.DOBRO.ambient 2.002: Three signatures? For one school drawing?
topic.DOBRO.ambient 2.x01: Mine, the headmistress’s and the building manager’s. The building manager signs that the drawing won’t fall off the wall.
topic.DOBRO.ambient 2.x02: And has one ever fallen off?
topic.DOBRO.ambient 2.x03: Once. Since then the building manager is on every form.
topic.DOBRO.extra 1.label: Comrade Headmistress
topic.DOBRO.extra 1.001: Who’s going to judge the exhibition?
topic.DOBRO.extra 1.002: Comrade Headmistress. She reads every label, even the one under the table.
topic.DOBRO.extra 1.004: Someone once left a model there without a label, and she found it. Since then everything has a label, even the things under the tables.
topic.DOBRO.extra 1.006: That’s thorough. Strict would be sending the unlabelled model home.
topic.DOBRO.extra 2.label: A good project
topic.DOBRO.extra 2.001: What do you think makes a good pupil’s project?
topic.DOBRO.extra 2.002: One that works, where the pupil can say why. Anyone can follow a template.
topic.DOBRO.extra 2.003: And when it’s different from the template?
topic.DOBRO.extra 2.004: Then the explanation has to be even better than the drawing. That doesn’t happen often.
topic.DOBRO.extra 2.006: It does. And you remember those longer than all the templates put together.
topic.DOBRO.extra 3.label: A new school
topic.DOBRO.extra 3.001: The school looks as if it’s only just been built.
topic.DOBRO.extra 3.002: It is new. The plaster is still drying, and the children are multiplying faster than the desks.
topic.DOBRO.extra 3.004: The estate is growing. A new block of flats every month, and a new class every September.
topic.JANA82.ambient 1.label: Did you draw that?
topic.JANA82.ambient 1.001: Yes. But it doesn’t look like the one in the textbook.
topic.JANA82.ambient 1.002: Maybe that’s exactly why it’s worth a look.
topic.JANA82.ambient 1.x01: Comrade Teacher says the wiring in the textbook has been tested.
topic.JANA82.ambient 1.x03: I know. I tested it at home and it works. It’s just that nobody knows yet.
topic.JANA82.ambient 2.label: What does it improve?
topic.JANA82.ambient 2.001: There’s less hiss, and you can still hear the whole broadcast.
topic.JANA82.ambient 2.002: Even in the evening, when tuning is at its worst?
topic.JANA82.ambient 2.x01: Especially in the evening. In the evening the airwaves are crowded and the weak stations get lost.
topic.JANA82.ambient 2.x02: With my wiring they don’t get lost. It’s different from the template.
topic.JANA82.extra 1.label: The radio at home
topic.JANA82.extra 1.001: Have you got a radio at home?
topic.JANA82.extra 1.002: We have. An old one with a green eye. When Dad switches it on, the eye slowly lights up.
topic.JANA82.extra 1.003: I’ve worked out why it hisses in the evenings. But I haven’t told Dad yet.
topic.JANA82.extra 1.005: Because he’d want me to fix it. And then I’d have to know how to put it back together too.
topic.JANA82.extra 2.label: The exhibition
topic.JANA82.extra 2.002: A bit. I’m showing the one that follows the template. That can’t go wrong.
topic.JANA82.extra 2.004: That’s under the template. It’s safe there.
topic.JANA82.extra 2.005: Safe, but nobody will see it.
topic.JANA82.extra 3.label: The second schematic
topic.JANA82.extra 3.001: Are you drawing that second schematic yet?
topic.JANA82.extra 3.002: I am. This time my own way from the start, and I’m writing the notes in the margin straight away.
topic.JANA82.extra 3.003: So you don’t forget why it works?
topic.JANA82.extra 3.004: No. So whoever reads it knows too. I understood that thanks to you.
topic.LIDA.ambient 1.label: When is the premiere?
topic.LIDA.ambient 1.003: Then it’ll be the premiere of a completely new work.
topic.LIDA.ambient 1.x01: And who’s going to write it?
topic.LIDA.ambient 1.x02: Rudo, right there on stage. He’s already got the first line.
topic.LIDA.ambient 2.label: How many costumes?
topic.LIDA.ambient 2.001: Six actors and four coats. And two intervals for changing.
topic.LIDA.ambient 2.002: So someone will be doing the second act in a jumper.
topic.LIDA.ambient 2.x01: Rudo will be in the jumper. He always feels cold on stage when he forgets his lines.
topic.LIDA.ambient 2.x03: The audience is from Ivanka. They know that jumper and give it its own round of applause.
topic.LIDA.extra 1.label: What’s the play about?
topic.LIDA.extra 1.001: What are you actually rehearsing in the hall?
topic.LIDA.extra 1.002: A play about a mayor who promises at the start that everything will turn out fine. The rest of the play he spends fixing what goes wrong.
topic.LIDA.extra 1.004: For the audience. For me it’s a tragedy about buttons.
topic.LIDA.extra 1.006: The mayor has twelve buttons on his coat. By the premiere I have to find at least eight.
topic.LIDA.extra 2.label: Rudo’s stage fright
topic.LIDA.extra 2.001: Is Mr Pavlík always so… enthusiastic?
topic.LIDA.extra 2.002: On stage. Backstage he hides behind a flat and waits until I call him.
topic.LIDA.extra 2.003: Once he stood there so long that we locked him in the hall, forest and all.
topic.LIDA.extra 2.005: He rehearsed all night. By morning he knew his whole part. He still had the script back then.
topic.MARTA82.ambient 1.label: What do you record?
topic.MARTA82.ambient 1.001: Everything that came in and everything that went out. Then, when something needs finding, it’s easier to breathe.
topic.MARTA82.ambient 1.002: I should introduce that in my workshop too.
topic.MARTA82.ambient 1.x01: Do. But start with what you no longer have. That’s the longest list.
topic.MARTA82.ambient 1.x02: That would take me until Christmas.
topic.MARTA82.ambient 1.x03: It took me two years here. Now the only thing missing is one key to the boiler room.
topic.MARTA82.ambient 2.label: I’m in a hurry
topic.MARTA82.ambient 2.001: Then tell me exactly what you need. That’s quicker than explaining to me that you’re in a hurry.
topic.MARTA82.ambient 2.x01: See? We’ve already saved two minutes.
topic.MARTA82.ambient 2.x02: Lucky you don’t write the minutes down.
topic.MARTA82.extra 1.label: Tóno’s aeroplane
topic.MARTA82.extra 1.002: It is. I put it on the top shelf so nobody sits on it.
topic.MARTA82.extra 1.003: Did you record it in the inventory book?
topic.MARTA82.extra 1.004: In pencil. It’s somebody else’s property and I’m only minding it. In pen it would become ours.
topic.MARTA82.extra 2.label: So much paperwork
topic.MARTA82.extra 2.001: Doesn’t all this paperwork bother you?
topic.MARTA82.extra 2.002: Not when it makes sense. A requisition slip says who took what and why. That’s order, not torment.
topic.MARTA82.extra 2.004: When someone wants three signatures for one screw. A form like that I send straight back.
topic.MIRA60.ambient 1.label: What is an exception?
topic.MIRA60.ambient 1.001: Something that doesn’t fit the model. That doesn’t mean it doesn’t exist.
topic.MIRA60.ambient 1.x01: That’s why I won’t throw you out. I’ll note you down alongside, like everything that doesn’t fit.
topic.MIRA60.ambient 1.x03: Alongside the original data, in the margin. My margins are written up more densely than my pages.
topic.MIRA60.ambient 2.label: Why don’t you ask me anything?
topic.MIRA60.ambient 2.001: I ask about what I can verify. The rest I leave open.
topic.MIRA60.ambient 2.002: Then that’ll run in our family.
topic.MIRA60.ambient 2.x02: That’s one of those questions you leave open.
topic.MIRA60.ambient 2.x03: Fine. But don’t think I’ll forget to ask about that family.
topic.MIRA60.extra 1.label: Little Zuzka
topic.MIRA60.extra 1.001: That little Zuzka from the park turns up everywhere I go.
topic.MIRA60.extra 1.002: She does that to everyone. Even to people who don’t know they need someone to show them the way.
topic.MIRA60.extra 1.003: Yesterday she asked me where I put the time I measure.
topic.MIRA60.extra 1.004: And what did you tell her?
topic.MIRA60.extra 1.005: The truth. That I write it down so it doesn’t get lost.
topic.MIRA60.extra 1.006: And was that enough for her?
topic.MIRA60.extra 1.007: No. She wanted to see the notebook. So I showed her the page with her hopscotch.
topic.MIRA60.extra 2.label: Measuring in the hut
topic.MIRA60.extra 2.001: What exactly are you measuring in that hut?
topic.MIRA60.extra 2.002: Time, in several places at once. And differences that shouldn’t be there.
topic.MIRA60.extra 2.004: They are. That’s why I note them alongside. What doesn’t fit, we write alongside, not over the original data.
topic.MIRA60.extra 2.005: Even when it looks like a mistake?
topic.MIRA60.extra 2.006: Then most of all. I can always throw it away. I can’t bring it back.
topic.MIRA60.extra 3.label: Mr Bielik
topic.MIRA60.extra 3.001: Mr Bielik speaks of you with great respect.
topic.MIRA60.extra 3.002: Oto speaks of everything with respect. Even of a screw that’s rolled under the table.
topic.MIRA60.extra 3.004: That he measures first and talks afterwards. That’s why he’s so good to work with.
topic.OTO.ambient 1.label: What is ZVON for?
topic.OTO.ambient 1.001: It was meant to compare clocks in several places at once. And then yesterday spoke to us.
topic.OTO.ambient 1.002: And you didn’t run out of the workshop?
topic.OTO.ambient 1.x01: Only then did we get a fright.
topic.OTO.ambient 1.x02: And what did yesterday tell you?
topic.OTO.ambient 1.x03: That I’d forgotten to switch off the soldering iron. It was right.
topic.OTO.ambient 2.label: Isn’t it dangerous?
topic.OTO.ambient 2.001: What’s dangerous is thinking we know everything. The machine itself doesn’t think that.
topic.OTO.ambient 2.002: In the future I know of one that does.
topic.OTO.ambient 2.x02: A person with a machine. That’s worse than either on its own.
topic.OTO.ambient 2.x03: Then someone should teach them to measure first and talk afterwards.
topic.OTO.extra 1.001: Why have you got four alarm clocks in your workshop?
topic.OTO.extra 1.002: I’m comparing them. Each one runs a little differently, and I want to know why.
topic.OTO.extra 1.004: None. But two of them are wrong in the same way, and that’s already information.
topic.OTO.extra 1.006: That one rings. It’s here so I don’t forget lunch.
topic.OTO.extra 2.label: My shoes
topic.OTO.extra 2.001: I’ve noticed you looking at my shoes.
topic.OTO.extra 2.002: First I look, then I speak. I’ve never seen soles like that.
topic.OTO.extra 2.004: Mine are work shoes too. And yet nobody turns round to look at me.
topic.OTO.extra 2.006: No. Just don’t stand near Mrs Kovárová any longer than you have to.
topic.OTO.extra 3.label: Working with Mira
topic.OTO.extra 3.001: What’s it like working with Mira?
topic.OTO.extra 3.002: Fast. She finishes my sentence before I’ve started it.
topic.OTO.extra 3.004: I mind when she finishes it better. And she often does.
topic.OTO82.ambient 1.label: You remember me?
topic.OTO82.ambient 1.001: In Ivanka you asked about the future. Now I’m watching it in my own grandson.
topic.OTO82.ambient 1.002: And I haven’t aged a day since.
topic.OTO82.ambient 1.003: I noticed. You’ve even got the same jacket.
topic.OTO82.ambient 1.x01: I’ve been through three since then. And you haven’t lost a single button.
topic.OTO82.ambient 1.x03: Then don’t lend them to anyone. Not even me.
topic.OTO82.ambient 2.label: Does Tóno help you?
topic.OTO82.ambient 2.001: He helps. Let him try things out and then explain them. But I approve the making of things and I sign the papers.
topic.OTO82.ambient 2.002: And does Tóno agree with that?
topic.OTO82.ambient 2.x01: He agrees until he needs a signature for something of his own. Then he haggles like a market trader.
topic.OTO82.ambient 2.x03: According to him, he does. But I do the signing, so he only thinks he’s won.
topic.OTO82.extra 1.label: The technical club
topic.OTO82.extra 1.001: You run a technical club here?
topic.OTO82.extra 1.002: I help. The children have the ideas and I have the pliers. Together that makes a club.
topic.OTO82.extra 1.003: And what are you making at the moment?
topic.OTO82.extra 1.004: A radio, a lamp and one aeroplane that won’t take off. That’s Tóno’s.
topic.OTO82.extra 1.006: That’s what he says too. He gets it from me.
topic.OTO82.extra 2.label: Memories of Ivanka
topic.OTO82.extra 2.002: The workshop, Mira, and you. You most of all, because you vanished without saying goodbye.
topic.OTO82.extra 2.003: I’m sorry. I was in a hurry.
topic.OTO82.extra 2.004: You’ve been in a hurry for twenty years. This time at least say goodbye.
topic.OTO82.extra 3.label: The estate
topic.OTO82.extra 3.001: What’s life like for you here on the estate?
topic.OTO82.extra 3.002: They’re building everywhere. In the morning it’s mud, in the evening there’s a new block.
topic.OTO82.extra 3.003: The blocks are all the same, only the numbers differ. The first week I kept ringing the neighbour’s bell.
topic.OTO82.extra 3.004: You’ll get used to it. In a few years it’ll be all green round here.
topic.OTO82.extra 3.005: You say that as if you knew.
topic.OTO82.extra 3.006: I have an inkling. And you do know where I come from.
topic.POSTA.ambient 1.label: What does a stamp confirm?
topic.POSTA.ambient 1.001: That the document was here at the post office today. Whether it’s true is for someone wiser to judge.
topic.POSTA.ambient 1.x01: I rarely hear that, if I may say so. Most people want the stamp to confirm they’re right.
topic.POSTA.ambient 1.x03: A stamp only knows the date, if you please. Everyone has to bring the truth with them.
topic.POSTA.ambient 2.label: Is your pigeon a carrier pigeon?
topic.POSTA.ambient 2.001: Béla is not a service pigeon. He is my private joy, with wings.
topic.POSTA.ambient 2.002: And does he ever carry letters?
topic.POSTA.ambient 2.x01: The odd note to the neighbour, when I’m out of sugar. He is not permitted to carry official post.
topic.POSTA.ambient 2.x03: He hasn’t got a service cap. And if he got one, he’d want a service dovecote too.
topic.POSTA.extra 1.label: Telegrams
topic.POSTA.extra 1.001: Do people send telegrams from here too?
topic.POSTA.extra 1.002: Regularly, if you please. You pay by the word, so people are very brief in telegrams.
topic.POSTA.extra 1.003: The shortest one I ever sent had two words: ARRIVING TOMORROW.
topic.POSTA.extra 1.005: He did. A week later. He didn’t send a correction – every word costs money.
topic.POSTA.extra 2.label: Stamps
topic.POSTA.extra 2.001: How many rubber stamps have you actually got here?
topic.POSTA.extra 2.002: Seven, if you please. Each one confirms something different.
topic.POSTA.extra 2.003: And which one is your favourite?
topic.POSTA.extra 2.004: The date stamp. Every day it tells the truth – I just mustn’t forget to change it.
topic.RUDO.ambient 1.label: What’s your part?
topic.RUDO.ambient 1.001: I make my entrance and cry out that everything will turn out fine!
topic.RUDO.ambient 1.002: I’d like to hear that off stage too, right now.
topic.RUDO.ambient 1.x01: Off stage I can’t say it. Off stage something always goes wrong.
topic.RUDO.ambient 1.x03: Such as losing my script. But on stage I’m convincing!
topic.RUDO.ambient 2.label: Do you get stage fright?
topic.RUDO.ambient 2.001: Me? Never! It’s only my knees that rehearse a performance of their own.
topic.RUDO.ambient 2.002: Just make sure they don’t go off on tour without you.
topic.RUDO.ambient 2.x01: Lída has forbidden it. The knees, the script and the hat all stay in Ivanka!
topic.RUDO.ambient 2.x03: I go wherever my knees go. We’re one company.
topic.RUDO.extra 1.label: Off stage
topic.RUDO.extra 1.001: What do you do when you’re not acting?
topic.RUDO.extra 1.002: I weigh grain at the cooperative. Quietly. There’s no shouting there.
topic.RUDO.extra 1.004: On stage I’m a king. At the scales I’m just Rudo. And Rudo says very little.
topic.RUDO.extra 1.005: And which of them is the real one?
topic.RUDO.extra 1.006: The one answering you right now. But don’t tell the audience!
topic.RUDO.extra 2.label: The little prompter
topic.RUDO.extra 2.001: They say the whole of Ivanka knows your first line.
topic.RUDO.extra 2.002: Not the whole of it! But little Zuzka from the park knows it better than I do. And says it with more conviction!
topic.RUDO.extra 2.003: Every day she stands in the doorway of the hall and whispers it to me when I forget.
topic.RUDO.extra 2.004: So you’ve got your own prompter.
topic.RUDO.extra 2.005: The smallest in the district. And the only one who doesn’t ask for a fee.
topic.RUZENA.ambient 1.label: What have you got today?
topic.RUZENA.ambient 1.001: What you can see. What you can’t see, ask about.
topic.RUZENA.ambient 1.002: And if I ask about something you haven’t got?
topic.RUZENA.ambient 1.x01: Then I’ll tell you when it’ll come in. And if I don’t know, I’ll tell you who does.
topic.RUZENA.ambient 1.x03: The driver who brings the deliveries. He knows everything a day before I do.
topic.RUZENA.ambient 2.label: How long does a jar like that last?
topic.RUZENA.ambient 2.001: A good jar lasts for years. As long as you don’t lose it.
topic.RUZENA.ambient 2.x01: Hiding, but also writing down where. Most jars get lost in the cellar.
topic.RUZENA.ambient 2.x03: People put them away down there so well that only their grandchildren find them.
topic.RUZENA.extra 1.002: Everyone who buys bread rolls. The rest I know by their bags.
topic.RUZENA.extra 1.004: A string bag means this block, a plastic bag the one next door. And anyone with a basket is from old Dúbravka.
topic.RUZENA.extra 1.005: And how do you know me?
topic.RUZENA.extra 1.006: By your empty hands. I remember those best – they always ask about something.
topic.RUZENA.extra 2.001: How many bottles do people bring back to you a day?
topic.RUZENA.extra 2.002: It varies. Most on Mondays. In the morning there’s a queue of people with bottles right out to the door.
topic.RUZENA.extra 2.003: And which ones come back most often?
topic.RUZENA.extra 2.004: Milk bottles. People drink milk all the time, even when there’s nothing to celebrate.
topic.RUZENA.extra 3.label: The smell of oranges
topic.RUZENA.extra 3.001: It smells of oranges in here.
topic.RUZENA.extra 3.002: They came in this morning. By ten the whole estate knew.
topic.RUZENA.extra 3.003: How did they find out so quickly?
topic.RUZENA.extra 3.004: The neighbour from the first entrance saw them from her balcony. She’s faster than the radio.
topic.SIMON.ambient 1.label: Why a lime tree?
topic.SIMON.ambient 1.001: Because one day someone will be glad to sit under it.
topic.SIMON.ambient 1.002: Decades ahead. I plan about as far as Friday.
topic.SIMON.ambient 1.x01: Soup you plan until Friday. A tree you plant for two generations.
topic.SIMON.ambient 1.x02: And if it doesn’t work out?
topic.SIMON.ambient 1.x03: Then at least we tried. The lime starts all over again every spring too.
topic.SIMON.ambient 2.label: Why does the cart come this way?
topic.SIMON.ambient 2.001: People take the shortest route. A young tree can’t defend itself yet.
